title: Unique identifier linking through account registration
description: Homeowner provides unique identifiers (email, username, etc.) during account registration, enabling linking of all subsequent data flows to this individual.
assumptions: Account registration requires unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier linking through camera/sensor data
description: Camera and sensor data may contain quasi-identifiers (location, time, device characteristics) that can be combined to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Camera/sensor data includes metadata that can serve as quasi-identifiers

title: Profiling individual through camera/sensor data analysis
description: Home Hub may analyze camera/sensor data patterns to profile the homeowner's behavior, routines, and preferences, linking this profiled data to the individual.
assumptions: System performs behavioral analysis on collected data

title: Processing of identified data during account registration
description: Homeowner's personally identifiable information is explicitly requested and processed during account creation and camera/sensor enrollment.
assumptions: Registration process requires PII collection

title: Identifier processing in camera/sensor enrollment
description: Camera and sensor enrollment may involve processing unique identifiers (device IDs, MAC addresses, etc.) that reference the homeowner's identity.
assumptions: Device enrollment requires unique device identifiers

title: Revealing attributes in camera/sensor data
description: Camera and sensor data may reveal attributes about the homeowner (location, presence, activities) that support identification.
assumptions: Camera/sensor data captures identifiable environmental information

title: Excessive data type sensitivity in camera enrollment
description: Camera and sensor data may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic home automation functionality.
assumptions: Camera/sensor data collection exceeds minimal functional requirements

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: Camera/sensor data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is needed for basic home hub functionality.
assumptions: System performs additional data processing beyond core functionality

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of the extent of data collection, processing, and potential sharing during account registration and camera enrollment.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data practices

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Homeowner may have limited ability to set preferences or customize how personal data is collected, stored, and processed.
assumptions: Privacy settings may be limited or difficult to configure

title: Limited access to personal data
description: Homeowner may have restricted access to view, download, or manage the personal data collected by the Home Hub.
assumptions: Data access controls may be restrictive

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Camera and sensor data collection may exceed what is actually needed for the stated functional goals of the home hub system.
assumptions: Data collection is not strictly limited to functional requirements

title: Processing of identified access code data
description: The guest's temporary access code is processed by the Home Hub system, which may be considered identified data if linked to a specific guest identity.
assumptions: The access code may be associated with a specific guest account or identity in the system.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the access code is truly 'identified' data or just a temporary credential.

title: Revealing attributes through access code
description: The access code reveals that a guest is attempting to access the home, which is a revealing attribute about the data subject's presence and intent.
assumptions: The act of entering an access code inherently reveals the guest's presence and access attempt.

title: Data type sensitivity - access code collection
description: The access code may be more sensitive than functionally required, as it's a security credential that could be misused if compromised.
assumptions: Access codes are security-sensitive data that should be handled with appropriate protection measures.

title: Duration/retention of access code data
description: The access code may be stored longer than functionally needed, potentially creating unnecessary privacy risk if retained after the access event.
assumptions: The system may log or store access codes for audit or security purposes beyond what's immediately needed.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the actual retention policy of the Home Hub system.

title: Unawareness of processing by guest
description: The guest may not be fully aware of how their access code data is being collected, processed, stored, or potentially shared by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: Guests may not receive clear information about data processing practices when entering access codes.

title: Lack of control over access code processing
description: The guest may lack control over preferences regarding how their access code is processed, stored, or shared by the system.
assumptions: Guests typically have limited control over backend data processing once they enter credentials.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of unlocking the door, such as storing access codes longer than necessary.
assumptions: Data minimization requires collecting only what's strictly necessary for the access function.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the system actually collects more data than needed.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video clips uploaded to cloud storage may contain metadata with unique identifiers (timestamps, device IDs, user accounts) that can link data to specific individuals
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifying information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of video content with metadata attributes (location, time, device) can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals
assumptions: Multiple attributes in video metadata can be combined for identification

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video clips contain revealing attributes (faces, activities, locations) that support identification of data subjects
assumptions: Video content captures identifiable personal information

title: Small anonymity set in home surveillance
description: Video surveillance in a home context has a small anonymity set, allowing individuals to be singled out from others
assumptions: Home environment has limited number of individuals

title: Highly sensitive video data type collected
description: Video surveillance data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required
assumptions: Video data is more sensitive than minimally necessary for home security

title: Excessive data granularity in video
description: Video data is captured at a very fine-grained level of detail beyond what may be functionally needed
assumptions: Full video resolution captures more detail than necessary

title: Data propagation to cloud services
description: Video data is propagated to cloud storage services where it may be accessible by parties beyond the immediate user
assumptions: Cloud storage involves third-party service providers

title: Excessive party exposure to video data
description: Video data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (cloud providers, support staff, etc.)
assumptions: Cloud storage involves multiple access points and personnel

title: Unawareness of video processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware of the extent of video collection, storage, and processing occurring
assumptions: Users may not understand all data processing implications

title: Limited control over video data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how video data is processed, stored, and shared
assumptions: Limited user control mechanisms for video data management

title: Difficulty in rectification or erasure of video data
description: Data subjects may lack control to remove or rectify video data that is no longer relevant
assumptions: Cloud storage retention policies may limit user deletion rights

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data collection may process more personal data than actually needed for the stated functionality
assumptions: Full video recording exceeds minimization requirements

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be stored longer than functionally needed without proper retention controls
assumptions: Cloud storage may retain data beyond necessary periods

title: Linking through device/user identifier in motion alert
description: The real-time motion alert forwarded from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend may contain device identifiers or user identifiers that enable linking of data across systems.
assumptions: Motion alerts typically include device or user identification for routing and attribution purposes.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion alert data combined with other available data (e.g., location, time) could serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Motion data patterns combined with temporal and contextual information can create quasi-identifying profiles.

title: Processing of identified data in motion alerts
description: The motion alert may contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., user ID, device ID) that are processed during transmission.
assumptions: Real-time alerts typically require user identification for proper routing and notification.

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion alert data may include revealing attributes (e.g., activity type, time, location context) that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion data inherently contains contextual information that can reveal user behavior patterns.

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The transmission of motion alerts between Home Hub and Mobile App Backend could be observed by third parties, revealing that motion detection is active.
assumptions: Network communications between devices can potentially be intercepted or monitored.

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data collection
description: Motion data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected when strictly required for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Motion data can reveal presence, activity patterns, and potentially sensitive behavioral information.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Motion alert data may be propagated to other services or systems where it is not functionally needed.
assumptions: Data forwarded to Mobile App Backend may subsequently be shared with additional services.

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Motion data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (e.g., Mobile App Backend) that may be more than functionally necessary.
assumptions: The set of parties receiving motion data is known at design time and may include unnecessary recipients.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and transmitted to the Mobile App Backend.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into how motion data is used beyond the immediate alert functionality.

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed and transmitted.
assumptions: Users may not have granular control over motion data collection and sharing settings.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (motion data) may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of forwarding real-time motion alerts.
assumptions: The system may collect and process motion data beyond what is strictly necessary for the alert functionality.

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video clip stored in the cloud is identified data associated with a specific homeowner, and is being retrieved and processed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The video is linked to a specific homeowner identity in the system.

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may reveal personal attributes about the homeowner (e.g., location, activities, possessions) that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Video content contains observable personal information about the homeowner.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be perceived as more sensitive than strictly required for the playback functionality.
assumptions: Video data contains sensitive personal information about the homeowner.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: The video may be processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is functionally needed for simple playback (e.g., metadata extraction, content analysis).
assumptions: The system may perform additional processing on the video beyond playback.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if additional processing occurs beyond playback.

title: Homeowner unawareness of video processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, or accessed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not fully disclose all processing activities.

title: Lack of homeowner control over video processing
description: The homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular consent controls for video data.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the playback functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this system and video data processing exceeds functional necessity.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual system design and data minimization practices.

title: Video data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: The video data retrieved by the mobile app backend may be accessible to more parties (e.g., other services, third parties) than functionally necessary for playback.
assumptions: The mobile app backend may share or propagate video data to other systems.
uncertainty_note: Depends on backend architecture and data sharing policies.

title: Lack of homeowner access to video data
description: The homeowner may lack control in accessing the personal video data that is being processed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The system may not provide adequate access controls for the homeowner.
